name: Airtable
description: Airtable merges spreadsheet functionality with database power, enabling teams to organize projects, track tasks, and collaborate through customizable views, automation, and integrations for data management

tools.name: Create base
tools.description: Creates a new Airtable base with specified tables and fields within a workspace.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: Name for the new Airtable base, visible in the UI.

inputs.name: tables
inputs.about: Configurations for tables to be created in the new base; each table needs 'name' and 'fields'. Must be an array of table objects, not a stringified JSON. The first field in each table cannot be 'singleSelect' as it becomes the primary field. Select field choices must include both 'id' and 'name' for

inputs.name: workspaceId
inputs.about: Workspace ID where the base will be created. MUST start with 'wsp' prefix (e.g., 'wspXXXXXXXXXXXXXX'). Common mistake: Do not use user IDs (usr prefix), base IDs (app prefix), or other Airtable IDs - only workspace IDs work here. Get your workspace ID from Airtable workspace settings or via the List

tools.name: Create Comment
tools.description: Tool to create a comment on a specific Airtable record. Use when adding comments to records, mentioning collaborators using @[userId] syntax, or creating threaded comment replies. Supports optional parentCommentId for threaded conversations.

inputs.name: text
inputs.about: The content of the comment. To mention a user, use the format @[userId] (e.g., @[usrGISFlfA7l5F7kY6]).

inputs.name: baseId
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the Airtable base. This typically starts with 'app'.

inputs.name: recordId
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the record on which the comment will be created. This typically starts with 'rec'.

inputs.name: tableIdOrName
inputs.about: The unique identifier (typically starting with 'tbl') or the name of the table within the base.

inputs.name: parentCommentId
inputs.about: The ID of the parent comment for creating threaded replies. If provided, this comment will be a reply to the specified parent comment.

tools.name: Create Field
tools.description: Creates a new field within a specified table in an Airtable base. The action first reads the base schema to resolve the table and check existing fields, so it requires schema read access as well as write access.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: REQUIRED. The name for the new field. Field names must be unique within a table.

inputs.name: type
inputs.about: The type for the new field. If not provided, it defaults to 'singleLineText'. Types that can be created via API: 'singleLineText', 'multilineText', 'richText', 'singleSelect', 'multipleSelects', 'checkbox', 'number', 'percent', 'currency', 'date', 'dateTime', 'duration', 'phoneNumber', 'email', 'url

inputs.name: baseId
inputs.about: REQUIRED. The unique identifier of the base where the field will be created. Format: 'appXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX' (17 characters starting with 'app').

inputs.name: options
inputs.about: Type-specific configuration for the new field. Required for 'multipleRecordLinks' (must include 'linkedTableId' - the ID (format: tblXXXXXXXXXXXXXX) or name (case-sensitive) of the table to link to; if you provide 'isReversed' or 'prefersSingleRecordLink', they will be automatically stripped as the

inputs.name: description
inputs.about: An optional description for the new field. This can provide context or instructions for the field's usage.

inputs.name: tableIdOrName
inputs.about: The ID or name of the table within the base where the field will be created. Table IDs start with 'tbl' followed by 14 characters. Table names are case-sensitive and must match exactly as they appear in Airtable.

tools.name: Create multiple records (Deprecated)
tools.description: DEPRECATED: Use AIRTABLE_CREATE_RECORDS instead. Creates multiple records in a specified Airtable table in batches of up to 10; if a later batch fails, earlier batches may already have been created.

inputs.name: baseId
inputs.about: Required. The unique identifier of the Airtable base (e.g., 'appXXXXXXXXXXXXXX').

inputs.name: records
inputs.about: Required. List of record objects to create. Each record must have a 'fields' key containing a dictionary mapping field names to values. Field names are case-sensitive and can contain any Unicode characters (e.g., 'Тема Reels', '日期'). Field values must match their configured types in Airtable (e.g.,

inputs.name: typecast
inputs.about: If true, Airtable will perform automatic type conversion. Helps with: converting strings to numbers, creating new options for single/multi-select fields, automatically creating/linking records in linked record fields from text values, and type coercion for compatible types. Does NOT help with: text

inputs.name: tableIdOrName
inputs.about: Required. The table ID (e.g., 'tblXXXXXXXXXXXXXX') or the table name (e.g., 'Tasks').

inputs.name: returnFieldsByFieldId
inputs.about: If true, the returned field objects will use field IDs as keys instead of field names. Using field IDs is recommended for integrations that need to be resilient to field name changes. Default is false, which returns field names as keys.

tools.name: Create a record (Deprecated)
tools.description: DEPRECATED: Use CreateRecords instead. Creates a new record in a specified Airtable table; field values must conform to column types, null, empty-string and false values are omitted, and some values may be normalized before submission.

inputs.name: baseId
inputs.about: Required. The unique identifier of the Airtable base (e.g., 'appXXXXXXXXXXXXXX'). Use AIRTABLE_LIST_BASES to find available base IDs.

inputs.name: typecast
inputs.about: When set to true, enables automatic data conversion from strings to appropriate field types. For example, if a singleSelect field receives a value that doesn't match an existing option, Airtable will create a new option with that value. Also converts string numbers to numeric types. Default is false

inputs.name: tableIdOrName
inputs.about: Required. The table ID (e.g., 'tblXXXXXXXXXXXXXX') or table name (e.g., 'Tasks', 'Meal Plan') where the record will be created. Table names with spaces and special characters are supported. This is separate from baseId and must be provided. Use AIRTABLE_GET_BASE_SCHEMA to find table IDs/names within

inputs.name: returnFieldsByFieldId
inputs.about: If true, the returned field objects will use field IDs as keys instead of field names. Using field IDs is recommended for integrations that need to be resilient to field name changes. Default is false, which returns field names as keys.

tools.name: Create Record From Natural Language
tools.description: Creates an Airtable record from a natural language description using the table schema and an LLM-generated field payload. Typecast is enabled by default and can be disabled.

inputs.name: baseId
inputs.about: Unique identifier of the Airtable base, typically starting with 'app'.

inputs.name: nl_query
inputs.about: Natural language description of the record to create. Example: 'Add a task called Fix Login Bug, status In Progress, priority High, due date 2025-03-15'.

inputs.name: typecast
inputs.about: If True, Airtable will automatically convert string values to their appropriate types (e.g., string to number, date parsing). Enabled by default.

inputs.name: tableIdOrName
inputs.about: Unique identifier (typically starting with 'tbl') or name of the table within the specified base.

tools.name: Create records
tools.description: Tool to create multiple records (up to 10) in a specified Airtable table. Use when you need to add new rows to a table with field values. Rate limit: 5 requests per second per base.

inputs.name: baseId
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the Airtable base. Format: 'app' followed by alphanumeric characters (e.g., 'appHPvgqYXl3LNHXq').

inputs.name: records
inputs.about: Array of record objects to create. Each record object must contain a 'fields' property with the cell values. Maximum of 10 records can be created per request.

inputs.name: typecast
inputs.about: If true, Airtable will perform best-effort automatic data conversion from string values to the appropriate cell type. If false (default), field values must exactly match the expected type. Use with caution as it may produce unexpected results.

inputs.name: tableIdOrName
inputs.about: The unique identifier or name of the table where records will be created. Table IDs are recommended over names for stability. Format: 'tbl' followed by alphanumeric characters (e.g., 'tblUkxCONS303zkN7').

inputs.name: returnFieldsByFieldId
inputs.about: If true, the returned field objects will use field IDs as keys instead of field names. Defaults to false.

tools.name: Create table
tools.description: Creates a table in an existing Airtable base with a specified name, description, and field structure. Optionally returns an existing same-name table instead of creating one.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: The desired name for the new table.

inputs.name: base_id
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the base where the new table will be created.

inputs.name: if_exists
inputs.about: Options for handling duplicate table name scenarios.

inputs.name: description
inputs.about: An optional textual description for the new table.

inputs.name: reorder_message
inputs.about: Internal field used to track field reordering messages. This is populated automatically when fields are reordered.

tools.name: Delete Comment
tools.description: Tool to delete a comment from a record in an Airtable table. Use when you need to remove an existing comment. Non-admin users can only delete their own comments; Enterprise Admins can delete any comment.

inputs.name: baseId
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the Airtable base from which the comment will be deleted.

inputs.name: recordId
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the record within the specified table from which the comment will be deleted.

inputs.name: rowCommentId
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the comment to be deleted from the specified record.

inputs.name: tableIdOrName
inputs.about: The unique identifier (ID) or name of the table within the specified base that contains the record and comment.

tools.name: Delete multiple records
tools.description: Tool to delete up to 10 specified records from a table within an Airtable base. Use when you need to remove multiple records in a single operation.

inputs.name: baseId
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the Airtable base containing the records to be deleted.

inputs.name: recordIds
inputs.about: A list of unique identifiers for the records to be deleted.

inputs.name: tableIdOrName
inputs.about: The unique identifier (e.g., 'tbluIzIsxPIM2V3Y4') or the name (e.g., 'Marketing Leads') of the table within the base from which records will be deleted.

tools.name: Delete Record
tools.description: Permanently deletes a specific record from an existing table within an existing Airtable base.

inputs.name: baseId
inputs.about: Unique identifier of the Airtable base, typically starting with 'app'.

inputs.name: recordId
inputs.about: Unique identifier of the record to be deleted, typically starting with 'rec'.

inputs.name: tableIdOrName
inputs.about: Unique identifier (typically starting with 'tbl') or name of the table within the specified base.

tools.name: Get Attachment Info
tools.description: Retrieves attachment metadata and download URLs from a specified Airtable record field, including sizes, types, and thumbnails when available; attachment URLs expire 2 hours after retrieval. An empty result can also mean the field was not found or did not contain a list.

inputs.name: baseId
inputs.about: ID of the Airtable base containing the record.

inputs.name: recordId
inputs.about: ID of the record containing the attachment. Must start with 'rec' followed by 14 alphanumeric characters.

inputs.name: tableIdOrName
inputs.about: ID or name of the table containing the record.

inputs.name: attachmentFieldIdOrName
inputs.about: Field ID (e.g., 'fldXXXXXXXXXXXXXX') or field name of the attachment field to retrieve information from.

tools.name: Get Base Metadata
tools.description: Retrieves basic metadata for one Airtable base.

inputs.name: baseId
inputs.about: The Airtable base ID, beginning with 'app'.

tools.name: Get Base Schema
tools.description: Retrieves the detailed schema for a specified Airtable base, including its tables, fields, field types, and configurations, using the `baseId`.

inputs.name: baseId
inputs.about: The unique identifier for the Airtable base. This ID typically starts with 'app' and is followed by a string of alphanumeric characters. It can be found in the URL when viewing the base.

inputs.name: include
inputs.about: Optional list of additional fields to include in the views object response. Currently only supports the value 'visibleFieldIds' (for views of type 'grid' only). When specified, grid views will include a visibleFieldIds array showing which fields are visible in that view.

tools.name: Get Record
tools.description: Retrieves a specific record from an Airtable table by its record ID. Requires a known, valid record ID obtained from listing records or another API call - this tool cannot search or list records. Use the list records tool to find record IDs. Empty field values are not returned in the response.

inputs.name: baseId
inputs.about: ID of the Airtable base.

inputs.name: recordId
inputs.about: ID of the record to retrieve. Must be a real record ID obtained from listing records or another API call. Format: starts with 'rec' followed by exactly 14 alphanumeric characters (e.g., 'rec4YsVV8cU6V4EiT'). This tool retrieves a single specific record - to list or search multiple records, use the l

inputs.name: timeZone
inputs.about: Time zone for formatting dates when cellFormat='string'. Required when cellFormat='string'. Uses IANA time zone format (e.g., 'America/New_York', 'Europe/London', 'UTC').

inputs.name: cellFormat
inputs.about: Controls cell value formatting: 'json' for native types, 'string' for all values as strings. When 'string', timeZone and userLocale are required.

inputs.name: userLocale
inputs.about: User locale for formatting dates when cellFormat='string'. Required when cellFormat='string'. Uses BCP 47 language tag format (e.g., 'en-us', 'en-gb', 'de-de').

inputs.name: tableIdOrName
inputs.about: ID or name of the table.

inputs.name: returnFieldsByFieldId
inputs.about: If true, field keys in the response are field IDs; otherwise, field names.

tools.name: Get user information
tools.description: Retrieves information, such as ID and permission scopes, for the currently authenticated Airtable user from the `/meta/whoami` endpoint.

tools.name: List bases
tools.description: Lists a page of Airtable bases accessible to the authenticated token. If an offset is returned, use it to retrieve the next page.

inputs.name: offset
inputs.about: Pagination token for retrieving the next page of results. This is an opaque cursor returned in the 'offset' field of a previous list bases response. Pass this exact value to retrieve the next page. Do not construct or modify this value. Only present when there are more than 1,000 bases.

tools.name: List Comments
tools.description: Tool to list comments on a specific Airtable record. Use when retrieving comments for a record, with optional pagination support for large comment threads.

inputs.name: baseId
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the Airtable base from which to list comments.

inputs.name: offset
inputs.about: Pagination token to retrieve the next page of comments. If specified, the returned comments will begin at the specified offset. Obtained from the previous response.

inputs.name: pageSize
inputs.about: The number of comments to return per page. Must be less than or equal to 100. Defaults to 100 if not specified.

inputs.name: recordId
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the record for which comments are to be listed.

inputs.name: tableIdOrName
inputs.about: The unique identifier or name of the table within the specified base containing the record.

tools.name: List records
tools.description: Tool to list records from an Airtable table with filtering, sorting, and pagination. Use when you need to retrieve multiple records from a table with optional query parameters.

inputs.name: sort
inputs.about: Array of sort objects to apply to records. Each object specifies a field and direction. Records are sorted by the first sort object, then by the second, and so on. IMPORTANT: Cannot sort by system metadata fields like 'createdTime' or 'lastModifiedTime' - these are metadata properties returned with

inputs.name: view
inputs.about: The name or ID of a view to use for filtering and sorting records. View names are case-sensitive. View IDs (format: 'viwXXXXXXXXXXXXXX') are more reliable than names and not affected by view renames. Use AIRTABLE_GET_BASE_SCHEMA to discover valid views. Note: this parameter is overridden if sort par

inputs.name: baseId
inputs.about: The ID of the Airtable base. Must start with 'app' followed by 14 characters.

inputs.name: fields
inputs.about: Array of field names or IDs to include in the response. If not specified or if ['*'] is passed, all fields are returned. Field names are case-sensitive and must match exactly as they appear in Airtable. The Airtable API accepts both field names and field IDs interchangeably in this parameter, regard

inputs.name: offset
inputs.about: Opaque pagination cursor token returned in the 'offset' field of a previous list records response. This value must be used exactly as returned by Airtable - do not construct, modify, or decode it. IMPORTANT: Do not pass numeric values like '50' or '100' - these are not valid offsets. Offset tokens a

inputs.name: pageSize
inputs.about: Number of records to return per page. Must be between 1 and 100. Defaults to 100.

inputs.name: timeZone
inputs.about: The time zone to use for formatting date and time fields. Required when cellFormat is 'string'. If not provided when cellFormat='string', defaults to 'utc'. Examples: 'utc', 'America/New_York', 'Europe/London'.

inputs.name: cellFormat
inputs.about: Format for cell values. 'json' returns structured JSON values (default), 'string' returns simple string representations. When set to 'string', timeZone and userLocale are required - if not provided, defaults will be auto-populated (timeZone='utc', userLocale='en-US').

inputs.name: maxRecords
inputs.about: Maximum total number of records to return across all pages. If not specified, all records matching the query will be returned.

inputs.name: userLocale
inputs.about: The user locale to use for formatting cell values (e.g., 'en-US', 'fr-FR'). Required when cellFormat is 'string'. If not provided when cellFormat='string', defaults to 'en-US'.

inputs.name: tableIdOrName
inputs.about: The ID or name of the table within the base. Table IDs start with 'tbl' followed by 14 characters. Table names are case-sensitive and must match exactly as they appear in Airtable. Can also be passed as 'tableId' or 'tableName'.

inputs.name: recordMetadata
inputs.about: Array of strings specifying additional metadata to include. Currently supports 'commentCount' to include comment counts on records.

inputs.name: returnFieldsByFieldId
inputs.about: If true, field keys in the response will be field IDs instead of field names. Recommended when working with field names that contain special characters or when building integrations that need stability across field renames. Note: The 'fields' parameter accepts both field names and field IDs regardle

tools.name: Update Comment
tools.description: Tool to update an existing comment on a specific Airtable record. Use when modifying comment text or updating user mentions using @[userId] syntax. API users can only update comments they have created.

inputs.name: text
inputs.about: The updated comment text. To mention a user, use the format @[userId] (e.g., @[usrGISFlfA7l5F7kY6]).

inputs.name: baseId
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the Airtable base. This typically starts with 'app'.

inputs.name: recordId
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the record containing the comment. This typically starts with 'rec'.

inputs.name: rowCommentId
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the comment to update. This typically starts with 'com'.

inputs.name: tableIdOrName
inputs.about: The unique identifier (typically starting with 'tbl') or the name of the table within the base.

tools.name: Update Field
tools.description: Updates a field's name or description in an Airtable table. Use this action to modify field metadata without changing the field's type or options. At least one of 'name' or 'description' must be provided.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: The new name for the field. At least one of 'name' or 'description' must be provided.

inputs.name: baseId
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the Airtable base containing the field.

inputs.name: fieldId
inputs.about: The ID of the field to update. IMPORTANT: Unlike data API endpoints, the Metadata API requires field IDs - field names are not supported. Field IDs start with 'fld' followed by 14 alphanumeric characters. Use AIRTABLE_GET_BASE_SCHEMA to find field IDs.

inputs.name: tableId
inputs.about: The ID of the table containing the field to update. IMPORTANT: Unlike data API endpoints, the Metadata API requires table IDs - table names are not supported. Table IDs start with 'tbl' followed by 14 alphanumeric characters. Use AIRTABLE_GET_BASE_SCHEMA to find table IDs.

inputs.name: description
inputs.about: The new description for the field. Must not exceed 20,000 characters. At least one of 'name' or 'description' must be provided.

tools.name: Update multiple records
tools.description: Tool to update up to 10 records in an Airtable table with selective field modifications. Use when you need to modify multiple existing records or perform upsert operations. Updates are not performed atomically.

inputs.name: baseId
inputs.about: The ID of the Airtable base containing the table.

inputs.name: records
inputs.about: List of records to be updated. Airtable's API limits updates to a maximum of 10 records per request. If you need to update more records, split them into multiple requests of 10 or fewer records each.

inputs.name: typecast
inputs.about: If true, Airtable attempts automatic data conversion from string values on a best-effort basis (e.g., '123' to 123).

inputs.name: performUpsert
inputs.about: Configuration for upsert behavior when updating records.

inputs.name: tableIdOrName
inputs.about: The ID or name of the table within the base where records will be updated.

inputs.name: returnFieldsByFieldId
inputs.about: If true, returns field values keyed by field ID instead of field name. Useful for integrations resilient to field name changes.

tools.name: Update multiple records (PUT)
tools.description: Tool to destructively update multiple records in Airtable using PUT, clearing unspecified fields. Use when you need to fully replace record data or perform upsert operations. Supports up to 10 records per request.

inputs.name: baseId
inputs.about: The ID of the Airtable base containing the table.

inputs.name: records
inputs.about: Array of up to 10 record objects to update. PUT destructively updates records, clearing unspecified fields.

inputs.name: typecast
inputs.about: If true, Airtable will attempt to convert string values into appropriate cell values.

inputs.name: performUpsert
inputs.about: Configuration for upsert behavior.

inputs.name: tableIdOrName
inputs.about: The ID or name of the table within the base where records will be updated.

inputs.name: returnFieldsByFieldId
inputs.about: If true, returns fields object keyed by field ID instead of field name.

tools.name: Update record
tools.description: Modifies specified fields of an existing record in an Airtable base and table; the base, table, and record must exist.

inputs.name: baseId
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the Airtable base containing the record to be updated.

inputs.name: fields
inputs.about: Fields to update. Keys are field names (case-sensitive) or IDs (fldXXXX recommended). Only specified fields are modified. Empty strings convert to null. Field names must match Airtable schema exactly (e.g., 'Call Status' not 'call status'). Use AIRTABLE_GET_BASE_SCHEMA for exact names/IDs. Date-only

inputs.name: recordId
inputs.about: The unique identifier (ID) of the record to be updated within the specified table. MUST be in Airtable's record ID format: exactly 17 characters starting with 'rec' followed by 14 alphanumeric characters (e.g., 'recABC123def456G'). Simple numeric values or row numbers are NOT valid record IDs. You c

inputs.name: typecast
inputs.about: Enables automatic data conversion and select option creation. CRITICAL FOR SELECT FIELDS: When false (default), Airtable rejects updates to single-select or multi-select fields if the value is not already an existing option, failing with 'Insufficient permissions to create new select option' error.

inputs.name: tableIdOrName
inputs.about: The unique identifier (ID) or the name of the table within the base that contains the record to be updated. Also accepts 'tableId' as an alias.

inputs.name: returnFieldsByFieldId
inputs.about: If `True`, API response keys record fields by field ID instead of name. Using field IDs is recommended for integrations resilient to field name changes.

tools.name: Update record (PUT)
tools.description: Updates an existing record in an Airtable base using PUT method. Use when you want to replace all field values, clearing any unspecified fields. For partial updates that preserve unspecified fields, use the PATCH-based update action instead.

inputs.name: baseId
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the Airtable base containing the record to be updated.

inputs.name: fields
inputs.about: Specifies fields to update. Keys are field names or IDs; values are new content. PUT method clears all unspecified cell values (destructive update). Empty strings are automatically converted to null to clear field values. For Date fields: use 'YYYY-MM-DD' format for date-only fields, or ISO 8601 for

inputs.name: recordId
inputs.about: The unique identifier (ID) of the record to be updated within the specified table.

inputs.name: typecast
inputs.about: When set to true, enables automatic data conversion from strings to appropriate field types. For example, converts string '123' to number 123. Default is false.

inputs.name: tableIdOrName
inputs.about: The unique identifier (ID) or the name of the table within the base that contains the record to be updated.

inputs.name: returnFieldsByFieldId
inputs.about: If `True`, API response keys record fields by field ID instead of name. Using field IDs is recommended for integrations resilient to field name changes.

tools.name: Update Table
tools.description: Updates the name, description, and/or date dependency settings of a table in Airtable. Use this action to modify table metadata without changing the table's fields or views. At least one of 'name', 'description', or 'dateDependencySettings' must be provided.

inputs.name: name
inputs.about: The new name for the table. Must be non-empty if provided. At least one of 'name', 'description', or 'dateDependencySettings' must be provided.

inputs.name: baseId
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the Airtable base containing the table to update.

inputs.name: description
inputs.about: The new description for the table. Must not exceed 20,000 characters. At least one of 'name', 'description', or 'dateDependencySettings' must be provided.

inputs.name: tableIdOrName
inputs.about: The unique identifier or name of the table to update.

inputs.name: dateDependencySettings
inputs.about: Configuration for date-based task scheduling in Airtable tables.

tools.name: Upload attachment
tools.description: Uploads a file attachment to a specified field in an Airtable record. Use when you need to add a file to an attachment field. The file must be provided as a base64-encoded string.

inputs.name: file
inputs.about: The file content encoded as a base64 string. This is the base64-encoded binary content of the file to be uploaded.

inputs.name: baseId
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the Airtable base containing the record.

inputs.name: filename
inputs.about: The name of the file including its extension (e.g., 'test.txt', 'document.pdf', 'image.jpg').

inputs.name: recordId
inputs.about: The unique identifier of the record to which the attachment will be uploaded.

inputs.name: contentType
inputs.about: MIME type of the file being uploaded (e.g., 'text/plain', 'image/jpeg', 'application/pdf').

inputs.name: attachmentFieldIdOrName
inputs.about: The field ID (e.g., 'fldXXXXXXXXXXXXXX') or field name of the attachment field where the file will be uploaded.

tools.name: Who Am I
tools.description: Returns the connected Airtable account's user ID and, when available, email address.
